newsitem.title: FRANCE: Snow, ice wreck end to French New Year holidays.
newsitem.headline: Snow, ice wreck end to French New Year holidays.

text.p: Snow and ice hit thousands of New Year holidaymakers on their way home in parts of France on Saturday, forcing many to wait hours for high-speed TGV train services heavily reduced because of the cold.

After the freeze closed the rail link between Marseille on the Mediterranean and Lyon in central France, some 10,000 travellers were forced to camp on Friday night in trains, cars and hastily-arranged emergency centres.
SNCF railway officials said traffic between Marseille and Paris had restarted, with one in two scheduled high-speed trains running after technicians worked through the night to unfreeze power lines.

TGV trains also restarted gradually from the Riviera capital Nice towards Lyon, but with only two departures due on Saturday. Ice had built up to 10 cm (four inches) in diameter on power lines, halting the electric trains.
Regional train services in the Rhone-Alpes were less affected and ran at around 80 percent of normal on main lines.
Extra trains were drafted in from northern France to help get some 30,000 to 35,000 skiers home from Alpine resorts, and the SNCF said rail traffic from the resorts was normal.
But direct TGV links between French provinces were cancelled to free up trains for the worst-hit areas. Travellers faced longer journeys because they had to travel via the capital.

Further west, several thousand stranded travellers spent Friday night in hotels and municipal halls in the Charente and Charente-Maritime area, with 2,000 passengers stuck at Bordeaux's main station overnight.
Runways at Bordeaux airport in the southwest froze over, causing long delays to flights.

Motorways were still closed around Poitiers and in the Loire, and south of Lyon the main A7 Autoroute du Soleil (Sun Motorway) was gradually reopened after up to 5,000 people were stranded overnight. Traffic was slow because of fog.

A three-month-old baby died of meningitis in hospital in Saint-Nazaire and doctors said the cold weather had weakened it and made it more vulnerable to the virus. But they said it was an isolated case.
Near Grenoble at the foot of the Alps, three people died on Saturday when two cars collided because of ice on the road.
In a Paris suburb, a 16-year-old boy died after falling through the ice on a lake.

Meteo France weather forecasters said the cold was likely to worsen on Monday and would last several days. The institute said temperatures would slip below minus 10 Celsius (14 Fahrenheit) in northern France early in the week.
